CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old male presents with upper respiratory infection after doing yard work/landscaping over the past week. Patient reports feeling really tired and short of breath. He believes he caught a cold that worsened. Shortness of breath occurred primarily with exertion, specifically when lifting and carrying heavy bags of soil. He got really winded during these activities. He felt a little warm but attributed it to exertion rather than fever. Patient denies currently coughing up anything but anticipates this may develop. He reports his elbows hurt quite a bit and his knees were pretty tired with some tension, which he attributes to the lifting of bags. Patient has received both COVID vaccines and denies any history of seasonal allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for shortness of breath with exertion, fatigue, elbow pain, and knee pain. Positive for feeling warm. Negative for current cough, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, type 2 diabetes, hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily for hypertension. Metformin increased to 1000 mg twice daily for diabetes. Robitussin for cough and ibuprofen/tylenol for fever and pain prescribed during this visit.

ALLERGIES
No seasonal allergies reported. No drug allergies discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient does yard work and landscaping. Attends barre classes with his wife to help relax. Attends house parties occasionally. Monitors blood sugar levels regularly during work week but inconsistently on weekends. Monitors blood pressure at home during work week but not on weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal with no fever. Heart sounds nice and strong. Scattered ronchi bilaterally on lung exam that clear with cough. Some edema of lower extremities noted. Pain to palpation of elbows bilaterally.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia. Hemoglobin A1C: 8 (elevated). COVID test ordered. Hemoglobin A1C to be rechecked in 4 months. Lipid panel ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection/viral syndrome: COVID test to be sent to rule out COVID. Expected to resolve in a couple days. Prescribed robitussin for cough and ibuprofen/tylenol for fever. Patient advised to call if symptoms worsen.
2. Depression: Currently managed without medication through barre classes. Patient declining medication or psychotherapy referral at this time; will reassess in a few months if desired.
3. Type 2 diabetes: Metformin increased to 1000 mg twice daily. Hemoglobin A1C to be rechecked in 4 months with goal to lower from current level of 8 to 6-7.
4. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Refill provided. Lipid panel ordered.
5. Follow-up appointment with doctor in 4 months.
